messages:
tasha: Quick bug from onboarding: our CLI and sample apps ignored a freshly rotated org key. They had REDWOOD_API_KEY set locally and REDWOOD_ORG_KEY mounted in their environment; service kept using the old mounted key after restart. repro below.

remy: ugh. do you have the minimal repro + log snippet?

tasha: repro: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=newkey; cluster has REDWOOD_ORG_KEY=old mounted; restart -> logs: "auth: using REDWOOD_ORG_KEY (old)"; requests 401 until pod removed.

adil: sounds like two issues: env precedence mismatch across SDKs (some prefer mounted org key) and cache/file change detection. we need a single resolver spec.

remy: proposed resolver order (RFC): 1) if REDWOOD_ORG present and REDWOOD_API_KEY_org exists prefer that 2) REDWOOD_API_KEY (primary) 3) REDWOOD_ORG_KEY (org-legacy) 4) REDWOOD_TOKEN (legacy) 5) file-backed creds/cache. emit WARN when any legacy alias is used.

adil: implementation notes: small shared package (js/py/go) that all SDKs vendor; on boot compute fingerprint for file creds (sha256 first 512b) and compare to cache to invalidate; expose client.reloadCredentials() and wire SIGHUP -> reload; add CLI flag --force-cred-refresh for CI.

remy: telemetry: add cred.resolution.source and cred.used_legacy=true/false so we can track migration. Also log chosen source on startup with low noise WARN when conflicts present.

tasha: docs: please add quickstart appendix for org/project scoping, example manifests for k8s rotation patterns (Downward API vs secret mount), and migration steps. customers keep getting tripped by mounted legacy keys.

ci-bot: CI queued for branch feat/creds-unify-222 (#4120).

docs-bot: created DOCS-6001 "Credential precedence & org-scoping guide" assigned to @maria-docs.

adil: I'll prototype the shared resolver and sha fingerprint logic. remy can wire into node + python SDKs and sample apps. tasha, ping on PR for quick review.

tasha: thanks all — getting parity here will cut a lot of onboarding noise. :raised_hands:
